title: Cop who shot driver of stolen vehicle not criminally responsible
article: An RCMP officer who fatally shot a man in Truro while hanging onto to the hood of a stolen vehicle has been absolved of any criminal responsibility for the man's death.

Felix Cacchione, director of the province's Serious Incident Response Team (SIRT), said in a news release issued Tuesday, that the investigation determined it was "reasonable for the officer to conclude his life was in danger and the use of his firearm to shoot the suspect was justified in the circumstances. Therefore, no charges are warranted against the officer involved."

Mitchell Anthony Speight, 22, of Amherst, died in the early morning hours of Aug. 10, 2019 after being shot by RCMP Const. Ben Goodwin from the hood of the stolen vehicle after being struck by the driver, who had accelerated to a high rate of speed. The officer struck his head when the vehicle crashed on Willow Street.
Goodwin, who has since recovered, spent a period of time in hospital after being placed under a medically induced coma to reduce brain swelling.
RCMP members had been investigating a complaint of a stolen vehicle from the Amherst area, when it was later spotted in Truro.

"Shortly thereafter, an officer observed the stolen vehicle behind another vehicle at an intersection," the SIRT report says. "When the officer approached the vehicle, the driver pulled forward, striking the officer, causing him to land on the hood. The driver sped off with the officer holding on to the wiper blade.
The officer discharged his firearm before being thrown from the hood of the vehicle. The driver sustained injuries that caused his death."
Speight had a long criminal history prior to the incident.
